subject: Energy
title: Radiation Exposure in Context
description: A fast breakdown of Radiation Exposure in Context for builders.

hook.text: Everyone is exposed to radiation daily—from cosmic rays, rocks, food, and medical scans.

buildup.text: Average annual background dose is about 2.4 millisieverts—your body handles this with normal DNA repair.

discovery.text: A chest X-ray adds 0.02 mSv. A CT scan adds 5–10 mSv. Living near a nuclear plant adds less than 0.01 mSv/year.

twist.text: A coal plant releases more radiation than a nuclear plant—trace uranium in coal escapes in fly ash.

climax.text: Airline pilots receive about 3 mSv/year from cosmic rays at altitude—more than most nuclear workers.

punchline.text: Radiation is everywhere—nuclear plants add almost none.

quiz.question: Which releases more radiation to the public—a coal plant or a nuclear plant?
